subject: SpeedPay throughput certification & handoff
messages:
From: Elliot Rhodes <elliot.rhodes@speedpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput baseline + acceptance criteria for onboarding

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team wants to surface two things before we finalize the Dedicated capacity contract: a short, repeatable throughput certification run and a firm latency/throughput acceptance criteria doc that our SREs can sign off on.

High level ask: can Redwood run a controlled load test against the model we'll serve (gpt-open-2.7b-quant) with production request patterns and provide a single-sheet summary showing:
- 95th/99th percentile latency at 8k and 12k concurrent tokens/day
- Stable throughput (tokens/s) under 2-minute bursts of +30% traffic
- Error rates (5xx/4xx) and retry behavior observed

Kara (cc'd) will share a sample production request trace and our desired SLA numbers. Our procurement needs the pass/fail evidence for sign-off. Can your team run this next week and share results?

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Rhodes
Head of Platform Engineering, SpeedPay
elliot.rhodes@speedpay.com

[Attachment: speedpay_sample_trace.zip (application/zip)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Rhodes <elliot.rhodes@speedpay.com>
Cc: Kara Lin <kara.lin@speedpay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Throughput baseline + acceptance criteria for onboarding

Elliot — thanks for the clear ask. We can run a focused certification window and produce the one-sheet evidence you described. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Pre-check: validate request trace + pin model variant (gpt-open-2.7b-quant)
2) Test 1 (baseline): 24-hour steady-state at expected QPS profile
3) Test 2 (burst): 2-minute +30% bursts repeated 6x across a 4-hour window
4) Observability: token-level latency histograms, tail latency (95/99), error taxonomy, and system-level metrics (GPU util, mem, queueing)
5) Pass criteria doc: 95th < 250ms, 99th < 400ms for inference-only latency at steady-state; error rate < 0.5%

I've attached a short runbook (speedpay-throughput-runbook-v1.xlsx) and the JSON config we'll use for the prod-like load generator. If those look good we can kick off Wednesday and share preliminary readouts by Friday.

I'll also loop in our SRE bench team for execution.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- speedpay-throughput-runbook-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- speedpay-load-config-prod.json (application/json)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: (none)
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: SpeedPay throughput cert — run coordination and responsibilities

Team — handing off SpeedPay certification run. External stake: SpeedPay (deal SP-4721) needs pass/fail evidence for procurement. Summary and asks below.

Quick summary from customer: they want a short certification with steady-state and burst scenarios against gpt-open-2.7b-quant using their production traces. Marissa will own customer comms; Ben will own test execution and measurement capture; Monica will validate telemetry and artifacts; Dev will run any model variant tuning (quant/kv cache settings) if we see tail issues.

Run schedule (tentative):
- Wed 2027-05-26 09:00 UTC: validate trace ingestion + environment prep
- Wed 2027-05-26 12:00 UTC: baseline 4-hour steady-state run
- Wed 2027-05-26 16:00 UTC: burst windows (6 bursts over 4 hours)
- Thu 2027-05-27 15:00 UTC: internal analysis and generate one-sheet
- Fri 2027-05-28 17:00 UTC: share results with SpeedPay

Acceptance thresholds (customer tentative): 95th < 250ms, 99th < 400ms, error rate < 0.5%. If we need to deviate we must document mitigation actions and customer sign-off.

Artifacts to produce: run logs (csv), lat histograms, GPU util dashboards (pdf), one-sheet summary (PDF + CSV), configuration used (JSON). Attachments will be uploaded to the shared run folder and linked to the HubSpot deal.

Ben — please confirm you can run the steady-state/burst flows with the provided config and estimate run time plus any infra reservations required.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 21:03:00 -0400
Subject: RE: INTERNAL: SpeedPay throughput cert — run coordination and responsibilities

All — run completed earlier today. Quick summary:

- Baseline (4h steady): passed at target QPS. 95th=210ms, 99th=360ms. Token throughput steady at 18.4k t/s for the configured batch size and KV cache profile.
- Burst test (6x 2-min +30% bursts): no service interruptions; brief queueing events observed during bursts resulting in 1.1% request retries (client-side). Retry behavior within acceptable customer tolerance but above our initial <0.5% target. Root cause appears to be transient queue depth on the routing layer — Dev adjusted per-request batching and we re-ran one burst to verify improvement (retries dropped to 0.3% on re-run).
- Errors: observed 0.12% 5xx tied to a misconfigured healthcheck on one replica (fixed mid-run).

Artifacts uploaded: speedpay-certification-results-20270525.csv, gpu-util-20270526.pdf, latency-histograms-20270526.png. Drive links above.

Next steps: Marissa please share the one-sheet with SpeedPay; Monica can you attach the telemetry pdfs to HubSpot record SP-4721? Dev — please include a short note on the routing tweak we applied for the post-run appendix.

Ben Carter
SRE Bench Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[Attachment: speedpay-certification-results-20270525.csv (text/csv)]
